# shadow/for-key-required-for-reorder

Require a `key` on `<For>` when items have an identity or the list is rebuilt.

`recommended` `has suggestions`

## Why

Without `key`, `<For>` matches rows by item reference. When the list is replaced with fresh objects (a refetch, a `.map()` that copies items, a server response), every row is destroyed and recreated: inputs lose focus and local state resets, even though row `7` is still row `7`. A `key` function tells `<For>` which rows are the same, so they are moved and updated instead.

## Incorrect

```tsx
import { useSignal } from '@shadow-js/core';
const [todos] = useSignal([{ id: 1, title: 'Write docs' }]);
const list = <For each={todos()}>{(todo) => <li>{todo.id}: {todo.title}</li>}</For>;
```

```tsx
import { useSignal } from '@shadow-js/core';
const [rows] = useSignal([{ id: 1 }]);
const [id] = useSignal(1);
const table = <For each={rows().map((row) => ({ ...row, selected: row.id === id() }))}>{(row) => <Row row={row} />}</For>;
```

## Correct

```tsx
import { useSignal } from '@shadow-js/core';
const [todos] = useSignal([{ id: 1, title: 'Write docs' }]);
const list = <For each={todos()} key={(todo) => todo.id}>{(todo) => <li>{todo().title}</li>}</For>;
```

```tsx
import { useSignal } from '@shadow-js/core';
const [names] = useSignal(['Ada', 'Grace']);
const list = <For each={names()}>{(name) => <li>{name}</li>}</For>;
```

## Suggestions

The suggestion adds `key={(item) => item.<field>}` after the `For` tag name and rewrites every read of the item to `item()` (a keyed row receives an accessor). It is withheld when the parameter is destructured, when only `.map(...)` triggered the report (no identity field to key on), or when the item parameter is reassigned.

## Disabling

Disable one line with `// eslint-disable-next-line shadow/for-key-required-for-reorder`, a block with `/* eslint-disable shadow/for-key-required-for-reorder */` and `/* eslint-enable shadow/for-key-required-for-reorder */`, or a whole file with the block form at its top. Disable it when the items keep their object identity across updates (the same objects are reused), so matching rows by reference already keeps them.

## Notes

- A list that cannot change (a module constant, a literal) is not reported: the rows are never rebuilt.
- Reported when the row callback reads an identity field (`id`, `_id`, `uid`, `uuid`, `key`, `slug`) of its item, or when `each` is built with `.map(...)` (new objects on every change).
- With `key`, the row callback receives an accessor: the suggestion rewrites `item` to `item()` in the callback.

## Messages

- `missingKey`: `<For>` rows are matched by object identity. Add `key={(item) => item.{{field}}}` so rows survive when the list is rebuilt.
- `missingKeyDerived`: `each` builds new objects on every change, so rows are matched by identity and all rebuilt. Add a `key` function.
- `addKey`: Add `key={(item) => item.{{field}}}` and read the item as an accessor.
